newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end broadly stable in modest volume.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end broadly stable in modest volume.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed broadly stable Monday in modest volume due to a lack of economic news in a trend players expect to continue Tuesday.

The only palpable movement of funds Monday saw some investors selling electricity utility stocks to position themselves in mining shares, they added. Both sectors have healthy growth prospects, but the electricity shares were likely to yield gains later than the miners, they said.
The General Index rose 0.41 percent to 2,153.0 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index edged down 0.02 percent to 3,082.9 points.
In a total of 1,720 trades, volume was 27.0 million soles ($10.2 million), almost half the average daily volume of last week, brokers said.

"Investors are restructuring their portfolios, looking at how long-term their profits are. At the moment there is a lot of diversification because many sectors have good prices," Julio Alcalde of local brokerage MGS y Asociados said.
Benchmark Telefnica del Per continued its run of modest volumes, ending stable at at 6.74 soles on 608,000 shares.
Electricity distributor, Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- dropped 2.33 percent to 1.34 soles, on volume of 268,000 shares.
Atacocha -- the leading polymetallic miner that has seen most gains in the sector's bull run -- rose 1.36 percent to close at 2.23 soles on volume of 322,000 shares.
